LibraryCatalog.target.cfg.ref: I7, I8, I9: discovery, recovery and mutations at 2 projects, 1 journal row at start, 2 mutations, 1 crash and 1 write stop, with a quiet environment (no other tab, no invalidation without a change, the workspace available)

LibraryCatalog.target-environment.cfg.ref: The same properties while another tab changes a root once and settles one journal row this tab is not replaying: 2 projects, 1 row at start, 2 mutations, no crash, no write stop

LibraryCatalog.target-workspace.cfg.ref: The same properties while the workspace goes away and returns three times: a replay fails with workspace-unavailable, the row is failed until the return re-arms it, and a row that failed on its third attempt stays failed. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, no crash, no write stop. To fit the pr queue it drops target's second mutation; with it the configuration takes about 80 s

LibraryCatalog.liveness.cfg.ref: RowEventuallySettled under LiveSpec (weak fairness of the replay and of discovery; the person, a crash and the workspace are not fair), no SYMMETRY: 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, 1 crash, the workspace away once

LibraryCatalog.today-ref-epoch.cfg.ref: Inventory L5: getProjectListing compares discoveryEpochRef after the pass settles and the listing lands in the query cache later; a pass started by a poll in between moves the epoch without cancelling the query, so a listing of the previous epoch replaces the catalog. Every invalidation after a storage change cancels the query, so the listing that lands still matches storage. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, 1 poll

LibraryCatalog.today-ref-epoch-safe.cfg.ref: Companion of today-ref-epoch at its bounds: under CatalogFence = ref every other property holds, CatalogReflectsStorage among them, so the window today-ref-epoch reports breaks the epoch rule and not the catalog's contents

LibraryCatalog.target-access.cfg.ref: I4, I18, AccessAnswerFenced and AccessMatchedById: 2 questions about 2 projects, each resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel whose earlier replies complete late, 1 invalidation with no change, and 1 mutation whose row starts recovering while a question reads; no row at start, no write stop. It drops the crash, which target-access-crash checks with one question; with both questions and the crash the configuration takes about 140 s

LibraryCatalog.target-access-crash.cfg.ref: The same properties with a crash: 1 question about 2 projects resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel, 1 invalidation, 1 mutation and 1 crash, which loses the open question while its replies are still in flight; no row at start, no write stop

LibraryCatalog.today-access-loop.cfg.ref: Inventory L8: getProjectRouteAccess (use-project-manager.tsx lines 2419 to 2545) re-checks the epoch after every read but the recovery set only on the found path; a creation of the asked project journaled while the configuration read is pending moves no epoch, and the loop answers missing while the tab holds a recovering row for the project. 2 questions about 2 projects resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel, 1 invalidation, 1 mutation and 1 crash; no row at start

LibraryCatalog.access-match-by-id.cfg.ref: I18 rules matching by id and generation: with a reply matched by question id alone, a question asked again about another project is answered from a read of the first project (p2 answered ready from a read of p1). 1 question resting on 1 read, 1 re-ask, 2 projects, no row at start

LibraryCatalog.env-double-replay.cfg.ref: Another tab settles one row this tab is replaying (OQ6, no lock): every property holds for this tab, which settles its own replay and accounts for the row. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 2 mutations, no crash, no write stop

LibraryCatalog.env-double-replay-witness.ref: The inherited risk beside env-double-replay, at its bounds: another tab settles a row while this tab replays it, so two tabs replay one row

LibraryCatalog.no-epoch.cfg.ref: D10 rules the epoch fence: without it a pass that an invalidation overtook (a mutation settling during the scan) replaces the catalog with what storage held before. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation

LibraryCatalog.export.cfg.ref: The target, labelled, at 1 project, 1 row at start, 1 mutation and 1 access question resting on 1 read, with no crash, no write stop and no workspace loss, so the graph stays under 1 MB (graphs.LibraryCatalog); adding the write stop alone takes it to 47,362 states

LibraryCatalog.wide.cfg.ref: Narrowed. The formal plan's wide bounds are 3 projects, 3 mutations, 2 crashes, 2 environment steps and 2 access questions; this configuration checks every property at 3 projects, 1 row at start, 2 mutations, 1 crash and 1 write stop, with a quiet environment (2,531,500 states, about 90 s). Adding one environment step to it, a journal row another tab writes or a root another tab changes, exhausts the runner's 1 GB heap
